tagline: A horseshoe of chalk bluffs, juniper and an old stage trail.
intro: Out of WaKeeney the byway runs south on US 283 into the Smoky Hills, named for the blue-gray haze they wear at sunrise and sunset. It turns east past Brownell, then north along the eastern shore of Cedar Bluff Reservoir and across the top of the dam, and comes back up to I-70 at Ogallah, sixty miles around.

The country is chalky limestone left by old seas, and the settlers built from it. Volga Germans and Swedes put up their churches in the southern part of Trego County, and the Swedish congregation hauled its cornerstone out of a canyon that already had names carved in its walls.

moments.title: Wilcox School
moments.text: A schoolhouse of native limestone built in 1886 that served Wilcox Township for sixty years and afterward became the clubhouse of a motorcycle club.

moments.title: Cedar Bluff
moments.text: Half a mile of 100-foot chalk bluffs above the reservoir, grown over with juniper that the settlers took for cedar, with a gravel road up to an overlook.

moments.title: Threshing Machine Canyon
moments.text: Once Bluffton Station on the Butterfield Overland Despatch, where a wagon train hauling a threshing machine to Salt Lake City was attacked and the machine burned. Travelers' names are still cut into the walls.
